title: In vivo analysis of noise dependent activation of white blood cells and microvascular dysfunction in mice
author: Eckrich, Ruan, et al.
materials: Since the regulation of the animals’ body temperature is significantly altered by the anesthesia, temperature homeostasis has to be carefully observed for the duration of sedation. To avoid hypothermia, animals are placed on a heated operation platform (MEDAX GmbH & Co KG, Neumünster, Germany). Furthermore, intensive eye care is of great importance. Therefore, repetitive application of eye ointment like Corneregel® (Bausch & Lomb Inc., Rochester, New York, USA) or Bepanthen® Eye and Nose Ointment (Bayer AG, Leverkusen, Germany) to avoid damage to the cornea throughout the course of anesthesia.

Approximately 15 min before microscopical analysis, fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-labelled dextran (Sigma, Deisenhofen, Germany; average mol wt 500 000; 0.5–0.75 mL of a 5% solution in 0.9% saline) and rhodamine 6G (Sigma, Deisenhofen, Germany, 0.5-0,75 mL of a 0.05% solution in 0.9% saline) were injected into the tail vein under local anesthesia (Emla® 25 mg/g Lidocain +25 mg/g Prilocain creme, Aspen Germany GmbH, Munich, Germany) utilizing a 0.3 × 13mm surgical canulla (BD Microlance™ 3, Becton, Dickinson and Company Ltd., Drogheda, Ireland).
Furthermore, rhodamine 6G is injected to visualize leukocyte-endothelial cell interactions as previously described [9].

In each chamber window, regions of interest (ROI) (north, east, south, west, middle) are defined. Chamber areas of insufficient quality due to non-adherence of the musculocutaneous tissue to the chamber window should be excluded from the investigation. A green filter (Excitation [Ex]:470 nm/Emission [Em]: 525 nm) is used for fluorescence imaging of the intravascular FITC-labelled dextran (Fig. 4) enhancing the contrast between erythrocytes and the fluorescent blood plasma. Furthermore, an orange filter (Ex: 545 nm; Em: 605 nm) is used for the fluorescence imaging of Rhodamine 6G accumulating in the mitochondria of white blood cells.Fig. 4Evaluation of segmental blood flow includes labeling the course of the respective blood vessel (A, red line 1), determining the vessel diameter (B, red line 1) and carrying out Cap Image's line shift diagram function in order to calculate red blood cell velocity (C, red lines 1-5). Original data in [11], reused with permission.Fig 4

Concentration-dependent response curves of arterioles branching from the MCA are established using the endothelium-dependent vasodilator, acetylcholine (ACh, 10−9–10−4 M; Sigma-Aldrich, Taufkirchen, Germany), the endothelium-independent vasodilator, sodium nitroprusside (SNP, 10−9–10−4 M, Sigma-Aldrich), and the vasoconstricting thromboxane mimetic, U46619 (10–11–10−6 M; Cayman Chemical, Ann Arbor, MI, USA) for noise-exposed and control animals as shown in Fig. 7
[11]. For analysis of response curves to vasodilating agents, arterioles are pre-toned to about 50–70% of the original diameter by titration with U46619.Fig. 7In cerebral arterioles branching from the middle cerebral artery noise markedly reduced endothelium-dependent vasodilation in response to acetylcholine. In contrast, responses to the endothelium-independent vasodilator, nitroprusside, and to the vasoconstrictor, U46619 (thromboxane A2 mimetic), remained unchanged (n=4 per group; 2-way ANOVA with Bonferroni's multiple comparison test). Reused from [11] with permission.Fig 7

steps.title: Sterilize chamber and instruments
steps.instruction: Autoclave or otherwise sterilize the custom dorsal skinfold chambers, titanium frames, fixing screws, sutures (ETHIBOND EXCEL V5 – USP 4‑0, 0.75 m) and all surgical instruments (e.g., Tuttnauer systec 5050 ELVD autoclave).

steps.title: Prepare and inject anesthesia
steps.instruction: Mix ketamine (0.1 mg per g body weight) and xylazine (0.01 mg per g) in 0.9 % NaCl (1 part drug mixture to 10 parts saline). Inject the solution intraperitoneally (IP).

steps.title: Maintain body temperature and eye care
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse on a heated operation platform (MEDAX GmbH & Co KG). Apply eye ointment (Corneregel® or Bepanthen® Eye and Nose Ointment) repeatedly throughout the surgery to protect the cornea.

steps.title: Confirm depth of anesthesia
steps.instruction: Check loss of positional, corneal and interdigital reflexes. If anesthesia is insufficient, give an additional 10 % of the initial ketamine/xylazine dose IP every 5 min until reflexes are absent.

steps.title: Depilate dorsal skin
steps.instruction: Shave the dorsal and flank skin with an electric razor, leaving a short hair layer. Apply Veet® depilatory cream, wait 3–5 min, wipe off cream and hair with tissue wipes, wash residual cream with warm water (37 °C), dry the skin.

steps.title: Disinfect skin
steps.instruction: Spray the depilated area with pre‑heated, alcohol‑free octenisept® disinfectant spray.

steps.title: Extend skinfold and position chamber
steps.instruction: Manually extend the dorsal skinfold and place the chamber frame over the double‑layer skin, aligning the window with a visible vessel branch under transillumination.

steps.title: Place primary sutures
steps.instruction: Thread two ETHIBOND sutures through the lateral holes of the apical chamber frame and retrogradely pierce them through the dorsal skinfold, ensuring the window will sit above a sizable vessel.

steps.title: Add stabilizing sutures
steps.instruction: Place at least two additional sutures at the apical and basal parts of the chamber to immobilize the frame on the skin.

steps.title: Insert fixing screws
steps.instruction: Using transillumination, locate the screw holes, pierce the skin anterogradely with a 1.5 mm Strauss cannula (DISPOMED), insert fixing screws through the cannula and pass them retrogradely through the skinfold.

steps.title: Mark chamber window borders
steps.instruction: Mark the external borders of the chamber window on the dorsal skin with a surgical pen (Securline® Skin Marker). Turn the mouse onto its lateral side with the sutured chamber frame facing down.

steps.title: Microsurgical tissue removal
steps.instruction: Under a ZEISS OPMI® 1 FC surgical microscope, remove the upper skin layer, the apical panniculus carnosus muscle and the two retractor muscle layers within the window area using microsurgical instruments. Continuously drizzle 0.9 % NaCl onto the exposed tissue to prevent drying.

steps.title: Close chamber with cover glass
steps.instruction: Place the opposite chamber frame with a 12 mm cover glass slip (Hecht Assistent) onto the prepared musculocutaneous tissue, fix the frame with titanium nuts and immobilize the cover glass with the retaining ring.

steps.title: Post‑operative analgesia and monitoring
steps.instruction: Provide tramadol in the drinking water at 0.1 mg/mL (Tramadol‑ratiopharm). Monitor and record each animal’s weight, health status and a score sheet daily. Exclude any animal with >20 % weight loss, signs of inflammation, or pain‑related behavior.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescent dyes
steps.instruction: Draw 0.5–0.75 mL of a 5 % FITC‑dextran solution (average Mw 500 000) and 0.5–0.75 mL of a 0.05 % rhodamine 6G solution, both in 0.9 % saline. Under local anesthesia (Emla® cream, 25 mg/g lidocaine + 25 mg/g prilocaine), inject each dye into the tail vein using a 0.3 × 13 mm BD Microlance™ 3 cannula.

steps.title: Position animal for imaging
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in an acrylic tube on the customized microscopy platform, affix the dorsal skinfold chamber horizontally to an acrylic glass frame with screws, and secure the setup to minimize lateral movement.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence videos
steps.instruction: Using an Olympus BXFM intravital microscope, define five regions of interest (north, east, south, west, middle) within the chamber window. Record a ~15 s video for each ROI with cellSens Dimension software, saving uncompressed AVI files.

steps.title: Analyze vessel diameter and RBC velocity
steps.instruction: Off‑line, open each video in Cap‑Image. For 3–4 vessels per ROI, measure vessel diameter (d) and red blood cell velocity (VRBC) using the line‑shift diagram tool; manually verify all automatic measurements.

steps.title: Calculate segmental blood flow
steps.instruction: Compute segmental blood flow (SBF) for each vessel using SBF = (VRBC / 1.6) × (d / 2)² × π (units: pl/s).

steps.title: Quantify adhesive leukocytes
steps.instruction: Play rhodamine 6G videos at 0.1× speed. Count adherent leukocytes manually with a mechanical hand counter (Roth Selection). Have two independent, blinded raters perform the count.

steps.title: Quantify rolling leukocytes
steps.instruction: Identify leukocytes whose velocity is reduced by >50 % compared with VRBC. Use the frame‑to‑frame velocity analysis tool to confirm the reduction and count the rolling cells.

steps.title: Dissect brain for cerebral arterioles
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse, remove the whole brain and immerse it in ice‑cold artificial cerebrospinal fluid to preserve tissue integrity.

steps.title: Isolate MCA and branches
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope, locate the middle cerebral artery (MCA) and its branches. Remove surrounding brain tissue with Vannas scissors and fine‑point tweezers.

steps.title: Transfer vessels to pressure myograph
steps.instruction: Place the isolated MCA with its branches into a pressure myograph equipped with dual micropipettes.

steps.title: Cannulate first arteriole branch
steps.instruction: Advance one micropipette tip into a chosen arteriole branch without directly grasping the vessel. Verify correct positioning.

steps.title: Secure vessel with nylon sutures
steps.instruction: Fix the cannulated segment to the micropipette using two loops of 10‑0 nylon suture (Alcon AG). Add a second suture on the cannulated part to prevent leakage.

steps.title: Cannulate opposite end
steps.instruction: Trim the non‑cannulated end of the MCA, then cannulate this opposite end with the second micropipette and secure it with a nylon suture loop as before.

steps.title: Set intravascular pressure
steps.instruction: Apply an intravascular pressure of 40 mmHg via the micropipettes, maintain under bright‑field microscopy, and equilibrate for 30 min.

steps.title: Perform pharmacological response testing
steps.instruction: Pre‑tone arterioles to 50–70 % of their original diameter using U46619. Then apply concentration‑response series of acetylcholine (10⁻⁹–10⁻⁴ M), sodium nitroprusside (10⁻⁹–10⁻⁴ M), and U46619 (10⁻¹¹–10⁻⁶ M) to assess endothelium‑dependent dilation, endothelium‑independent dilation, and vasoconstriction, respectively.
